stages.name: Labour market
stages.title: Supply of labour
stages.sub: What determines how many people are willing to work in an occupation.

steps.q: You already know supply is the quantity sellers are willing to offer at a given price. Nurses sell their time and effort to hospitals instead of a good. If the wage on offer rises, would more or fewer people be willing to take up nursing?
steps.right: More people would be willing to
steps.wrong: Fewer people would be willing to
steps.hint: Workers are the ones offering their labour, like sellers offering a good at a price.

steps.q: Plumbing pays £40,000 a year and warehouse packing pays £20,000, and both need similar effort. Which job will more people want to move into?
steps.wrong: Packing, since it is easier to get into
steps.hint: If effort is similar, which wage would pull workers towards it?

steps.q: Becoming a surgeon takes seven years of training, while becoming a shop assistant takes a day of training. Even if both paid the same, would the same number of people be able to switch into each job overnight?
steps.right: No, far fewer could become surgeons quickly
steps.wrong: Yes, people could switch into either equally fast
steps.hint: Think about how long it takes to gain the skills each job needs.

steps.q: Two jobs pay exactly the same, but one lets you work outdoors with flexible hours and the other is night-shift cleaning in a cold warehouse. Even at equal pay, will the same number of people want each job?
steps.right: No, more will want the outdoor flexible job
steps.wrong: Yes, since the pay is identical
steps.hint: Pay is equal here, so what else about the job could make people prefer one over the other?

steps.q: Job A pays less than Job B, but Job A has short hours, no weekend work and high job satisfaction. A worker weighs up the pay difference against these other differences before deciding. What is she comparing?
steps.right: The overall reward, pay and conditions together, of each job
steps.wrong: Only the pay difference between the two jobs
steps.hint: She is not looking at wages alone, she is weighing wages together with the working conditions.
